title: Balls, Races, Water, Ice
bigQuestion: Why does each kind of play need its own kind of place?

story.title: The Floor Changes
story.kicker: A class walks outside and feels the ground change under their shoes.
paragraphs: Room 104 leaves the gym in a line. The gym floor is smooth wood. Their shoes squeak on it. Two orange hoops hang above the ends of the floor.
The door opens. Now their shoes land on rubber chips. Then they step on grass. A girl named Priya stops. "The floor changed three times!" she says.

Mr. Dunn points across the street. A tall fence surrounds a red oval track. Next to it is a low brick building. "That building holds the pool," he says. "In winter, the park floods the tennis courts for skating."
Priya counts on her fingers. Wood for hoops. Grass for kicking. A red oval for running. Water for swimming. Ice for skating. "Every game has its own floor," she says.
story.think: What kind of floor is under your feet at recess? What games fit on it?

lessons.title: Stone Courts in Mexico
lessons.mainIdea: More than 3,000 years ago, people in Mexico and Central America built stone courts for a rubber-ball game.
reading: People in Mexico and Central America played a ball game long ago. They made the balls from *rubber*. Rubber comes from the sap of a tree. The balls bounced high.
Some rubber balls found in Mexico are more than 3,000 years old. They were found in a wet spring at a place called El Manatí. The mud kept them safe.
Towns built long stone courts for the game. Many courts had two sloped walls. The Maya, the Aztecs and other peoples all played on courts like these.

words.d: a bouncy material made from the sap of some trees
a flat place with edges, built for a game

look.prompt: Why do you think the builders used stone and not grass?

check.q: What were the old Mexican game balls made of?
check.why: The balls were made from rubber, which comes from tree sap.

check.q: Where were some very old rubber balls found?
check.why: Old rubber balls were found in a wet spring at El Manatí, Mexico.

check.q: What did towns build for this ball game?
check.why: Towns in Mexico and Central America built long stone courts.

lessons.title: A Meeting in London
lessons.mainIdea: In 1863, clubs in London formed the Football Association and wrote one set of rules for soccer.
reading: In England, towns and schools played many kicking games. Each place had its own rules. When two teams met, they argued about which rules to use.
On 26 October 1863, men from football clubs met at the Freemasons' Tavern in London. They formed the *Football Association*. By December they had written one set of rules.
The game played by those rules is called association football. Students shortened "association" into the word *soccer*. The field for the game is called a pitch.

words.d: the group formed in London in 1863 to write shared soccer rules
a short name for association football

lessons.title: Tennis on a Lawn
lessons.mainIdea: Walter Wingfield introduced lawn tennis in 1873 and patented it in 1874.
reading: Walter Wingfield was a British army officer. In 1873 he showed a new game. He showed it at a party in Wales. It was played on a grass *lawn*. He patented the game in 1874.
His first court was wide at the ends and narrow at the net. It looked like an hourglass. Soon players changed it into the long rectangle we know today.
In 1877, a club in Wimbledon held a championship. Wimbledon is near London. The matches were on grass. Women got their own Wimbledon singles event in 1884.

words.d: a flat area of short, cut grass
a government paper that says an idea belongs to the person who made it

check.why: His first court was wide at the ends and narrow at the net, like an hourglass.

check.why: The women's singles event at Wimbledon began in 1884.

lessons.title: Peach Baskets in a Gym
lessons.mainIdea: In December 1891, James Naismith made basketball for a gym in Springfield, Massachusetts.
reading: James Naismith taught at a YMCA school in Springfield, Massachusetts. Winter was cold and snowy. His class could not play outside. They needed an indoor game.
In December 1891, Naismith nailed two peach baskets to a balcony in the *gym*. The baskets were ten feet above the floor. Goals are still ten feet high today.
Naismith wrote thirteen rules for the new game. A school newspaper printed them in January 1892. Soon YMCAs across the country were playing basketball.

words.d: a large indoor room built for games and exercise
the Young Men's Christian Association, a group that built gyms and ran classes

lessons.title: The Race at Olympia
lessons.mainIdea: The ancient Greeks ran races on a long, straight dirt path at Olympia.
reading: Olympia is a place in Greece. Long ago, Greeks held games there to honor their god Zeus. Tradition says the first games were held in 776 BCE.
The oldest event was one foot race. It went one length of the *stadium*. At Olympia that path was about 192 meters long. It was straight, with no curves.
Our word stadium comes from that Greek race. Only free Greek men and boys could enter. Married women were not allowed to watch.

words.d: a place built for races and games, with room for people to watch
a place in Greece where the ancient Olympic Games were held

lessons.title: A Marble Stadium in 1896
lessons.mainIdea: The first modern Olympic Games were held in 1896 in a rebuilt marble stadium in Athens.
reading: In 1896, the first modern Olympic Games opened in Athens, Greece. A Frenchman, Pierre de Coubertin, worked hard to bring them back.
The races were held in the Panathenaic Stadium. It was an old stadium rebuilt in white *marble*. Its running *track* had very tight turns at the ends.
Today most outdoor tracks are ovals. One lap in the inside lane is 400 meters. World Athletics sets that size. It runs the sport around the world.

words.d: a hard, smooth stone, often white
a path with lanes, built for running races

check.q: How long is one lap in the inside lane of a modern outdoor track?
check.why: World Athletics sets one inside-lane lap at 400 meters.

lessons.title: From the Sea to a Pool
lessons.mainIdea: Olympic swimmers raced in the sea in 1896 and in a pool starting in 1908.
reading: In 1896, Olympic swimmers raced in the open sea near Athens. The water was cold and wavy. Swimmers could not see a line to follow.
In 1908, London built a *pool* inside its big Olympic stadium. It was 100 meters long. In 1924, Paris used a 50-meter pool with lane lines.
Women first swam in the Olympic Games in 1912, in Stockholm, Sweden. Fanny Durack of Australia won the 100-meter race.

words.d: a tank of water with a measured length, built for swimming
one marked path for one swimmer or runner

look.prompt: Where would it be easier to tell who swam fastest? Why?

check.q: Where did Olympic swimmers race in 1896?
check.why: In 1896 the swimming races were held in the sea near Athens.

check.q: In what year did women first swim in the Olympic Games?
check.why: Women's Olympic swimming began in 1912 in Stockholm.

check.q: Who won the women's 100-meter race in 1912?
check.why: Fanny Durack of Australia won the 100-meter race in 1912.

lessons.title: Hockey Moves Indoors
lessons.mainIdea: The first organized indoor ice hockey game was played in Montreal on 3 March 1875.
reading: Thousands of years ago, people in northern Europe made skates. They used animal bones. Later, skaters played stick games on frozen ponds.
On 3 March 1875, James Creighton set up a hockey game indoors. It was in the Victoria Skating Rink in Montreal, Canada. Players used a flat wooden *puck*, not a ball.
A *rink* is a sheet of ice with walls around it. National Hockey League rinks are 200 feet long. Chicago's Black Hawks joined the league in 1926.

words.d: a sheet of ice with walls around it, built for skating or hockey
a flat, round disk used in ice hockey
